THE JRA IS FALLING DOWN

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
With only 6 % of the City of Johannesburg’s bridges in a good condition – who’s to blame? Carte Blanche investigates.

Unique Selling Point:
- STORY CURRENTLY IN THE NEWS - BUT OTHER JOURNOS ARE REPORTING ON THE TRAFFIC DRAMA...
- WE UNCOVER THE CORRUPTION AND MISMANAGEMENT BEHIND THE CURRENT STATE OF JHB's BRIDGES
- VISUALS WILL BE SHOCKING
- WE HAVE ACCESS TO A RECORDING PROVING KICKBACKS AND IMPLICATING A VERY SENIOR OFFICIAL AT THE JRA
- GREAT OPPORTUNITY FOR CONFRONT WITH MAYOR HERMAN MASHABA AND A CHANCE TO DEMAND THAT REPORT HE PROMISED ALMOST A YEAR AGO - HE IS SO SET ON ROOTING OUT CORRUPTION BUT APPARENTLY NOT SO MUCH WHEN IT INVOLVES COALITION PARTNERS.....


Summary:
94% of Johannesburg’s bridges are in a fair to extremely poor condition. City Mayor Herman Mashaba would like you to believe he inherited the problem and that it’s the ANC’s fault.

We beg to differ. There is proof that Mayor Mashaba is not free from blame – he is in part responsible for the current situation.

We speak to insiders and experts to get to the bottom of the bridge fiasco, putting Mayor Mashaba on the spot.


Further information:
THE BRIDGE CONDITION STATISTICS ARE NOT NEW – 94% of BRIDGES HAVE BEEN IN A TERRIBLE STATE SINCE 2013!

JRA HISTORY RELATED TO MAINTENANCE
A 7 yr plan was done in 2013 to address the bridge situation. JRA engineers worked with SANRAL engineers to come up with a game plan to address the maintenance issues and implement a plan of action to do repairs where needed and to maintain the good bridges.

The city would need R700 000 per bridge to maintain the good ones. R4 million to bring the fair ones up to very good status. R15 million from poor to very good. R70 million from very poor to very good.

The JRA team under Sean Phillips and then CEO (not sure of spelling) had implemented a plan with targets in place – in 2014, 2015 & 2016 those targets were met.

ENTER MASHABA & COALITION GOVERNMENT
In 2017 & 2018 no targets were met. NOT A SINGLE BRIDGE WAS MAINTAINED OR REPAIRED. That budget is believed to have gone back to treasury. SO DEAR MAYOR MASHABA, YOU CAN’T BLAME THE ANC FOR THIS ONE….

During November 2016 there were massive storms and flooding in Johannesburg. 15 bridges were closed as a result. Today they are still closed.

WHY THE LACK OF ACTION?
Internal struggles to get tenders awarded to the “RIGHT” consultants and engineers. Links back to our JRA story and how coalition politics impacts on the running of the municipality and service delivery.

In the case of the 15 bridges that were closed in 2016, Mashaba will claim that an EIA needs to be done and a contractor needs to be appointed.

THIS IS NOT THE CASE – in an emergency situations, no EIA’s are necessary. The repairs for a number of the bridges could have been done internally by the JRA – the expertise and resources were available – but it seems tenderpreneuring got in the way of service delivery.

An example is the John Hlanhla bridge in Alex – it needs to have the embankment filled up and secured. Still hasn’t happened.

THOMAS CHONGA – ENGINEER & HEAD OF PLANNING: JRA – ALSO TAKES KICKBACKS
We are in possession of an audio recording where Chongo details & negotiates his kick back from consultants – he explains how it needs to be done. I am negotiating with the source to be able to use it on air – if not we’ll find ways of incorporating the allegations.

Chonga has managed to get 3 bridge contracts awarded to one company – OJM. This is irregular as the JRA used to rotate contracts between consultants – one for you, then one for you, then one for you. This isn’t happening any more.

As the head of planning, Chonga, has acted outside of his scope and interfered in Supply Chain Management. Rumour has it that he was dismissed from Ekurhuleni for similar mismanagement – need to confirm.

SIDE STEPPING TENDER PROCESSES
Since MAshaba’s coalition government has been in place no contracts have been awarded through the normal tender process. Apparently the tender specification are so ridiculous that no one meets the requirements – not even big companies like Stefanotti. This in turn opens the door for Regulation 32 – if no suitable contractor submitted a tender, the municipality may directly contract a contractor currently being used by another municipality. Ekurhuleni uses Khato Civils who were the subject of our last JRA story that exposed the irregular prepayment of R23 million that was made to them.

Even JRA employees raised concerns about the tender specifications being unrealistic, but it was pushed through.

Currently the JRA are claiming to come up with new strategies – yet new data has been generated. Even Gauteng Province has offered assistance to attend to the bridges and road maintenance, but the delays according to insiders are simply the allocation of contracts that stand to benefit corrupt individuals with in the JRA – the expertise and plan exists internally but is not being used.

M2 CLOSURE FOR REPAIRS
Mayor Mashaba is masquerading this contract as a display of his government delivering on promises, doing the maintenance and repairs that the ANC was incapable of.

They seem to have chosen the bridge that would draw the most attention and would also deliver the most contracts – ignoring bridges that could literally collapse any day.

QUEEN ELIZABETH BRIDGE – BRAAMFONTEIN
Traffic from the M2 is now being diverted along this bridge. This is a very bad move. The pictures tell a very dire story. Trains also move underneath this bridge, structural engineers have raised concerns, yet it has been ignored.

AND IGNORING BRIDGES THAT COULD REALLY MAKE A DIFFERENCE TO COMMUNITIES: MZIMHLOPHE PEDESTRIAN BRIDGE
This bridge gives school kids access from their neighbourhood to the school – it’s a 300m distance over the bridge. It remains closed because it is unsafe, they now have to travel a 9km distance to get to school.

VIUSALLY IT’s HORRIFIC! PEOPLE ARE GOING TO GO MENTAL AND WE ALL SHOULD BE REALLY CONCERNED ABOUT WHERE WE DRIVE… IT’s LITERALLY DISASTERS WAITING TO HAPPEN!!

Script:


TRAFFIC UPSOUND

VO: Joburg road users spend hours a day in heavily congested traffic. To make matters worse, most of the roads and bridges they use, are substandard.

LINK: But it appears even the Johannesburg Roads Agency is gridlocked – with delays on repairs, rehabilitation and the commissioning of new bridges – it looks like things might have to get worse before they get better.

VO: Work is underway on sections of the M2 motorway – the main arterial that connects all four corners of the city. It deteriorated to such an extent that in February, it had to be closed for repairs.

But JRA insiders feel, it’s a case of smoke and mirrors.

INSIDER: It will make sense to close M2 – because it will make big noise //every month you are getting media releases – there are bridges in Alex, Soweto and Randburg that are currently closed, prior M2 – why are they not being attended to.

VO: A number of bridges are seemingly not being attended to.

707 bridges are in a poor to very poor state. Another 143 are considered to be fair, while only 52 – that’s just under 6 % of the bridges in the JRA network, are in good to very good condition.

HERMAN: The city is 902 – 77 % bad conditions – drive under them at your own risk.

VO: City of Joburg Mayor, Herman Mashaba, acknowledges that there’s work to be done.

HERMAN: scary situation – but engineer going to look on regular basis- where am I going to find 6.5 billion…. overnight

VO: But the delays are more sinister than simply a lack of resources according to JRA Insiders like this former roads agency employee.

INSIDER: I think currently they don’t know what to do number 1, because bulk of their time they using for fighting for tenders.

VO: Our source explained, it’s all about who gets the job – and, the kickback.

What you are about to hear is a snippet from a meeting between a JRA official and a potential contractor negotiating a bribe. This is the voice of the contractor.

CONTRACTOR: We can wash it nicely, clean it – by the time it comes into your bank account you are able to justify it to tax man.

LINK: so while the city is diverting you off the M2 because of its condition – the irony is you are being diverted to other route that also have dodgy bridge in need of urgent attention.

PETER: This is no longer bad. This is darn dangerous – this is emergency work.

VO: Civil Engineer Peter Coetzee has done extensive bridge inspections around the city in recent years. He did a visual inspection with us on the Queen Elizabeth and Harrison Street Bridges in the city centre - connecting Braamfontein and Newtown. Thousands of cars cross over them everyday – even more so with some traffic diverted from the closed M2.

PETER: that crack is about a centimetre wide already – is you just have the wrong sort of earthquake, tremor or loading – this whole thing could come down.
DEVI: Would you be concerned
PETER: yes, this is serious.

VO: While there were parts of the bridges in dire need of repair - with sections where re-enforced rods are exposed to the elements. Coetzee explained that the bulk of structure was still relatively sound.

The JRA’s head of planning, Thomas Chongo, says they are aware of the state of these bridges.

T – we continuous monitor all the bridges we are concerned
D – processes urgent today or tomorrow not end of year
T – we look at it – if it becomes a threat – would closed it off
D – not ER
T – urgent – not Emergency situation as it stands.

VO: But it seems even when it’s an emergency it’s not always dealt with urgently at the JRA. In November 2016, extreme flooding hit Johannesburg causing havoc across the city – at least 9 bridges collapsed.

LINK: Bridges like this one – the Joe Nhlanhla Bridge in Alexandra were damaged, declared unsafe and closed. That was back in 2016… nothing has changed.

VO: Adolph Marema is the ward councillor for this section of Alexandra.

ADOLPH: 3000 to 4000 people passes – there’s more than 6 schools on the this other side // the taxi ranks are not this side – they are this side, so people from this side go this side to access to taxi rank, kids form this side goes to access schools

VO: After doing a visual inspection of this bridge, Coetzee believes it’s fairly stable.

PETER: There is not cracking, there’s been no movement, the concrete looks solid, there is no spalling or anything – except for the approach slabs and the ring walls which might need a bit of repair and the gabience that have fallen away – it’s fine.

VO: Marema points out, it goes beyond the structure and inconvenience – residents are not safe.

ADOLPH: once in a month we get reports of someone who has died, who has passed on, stabbed, mugged, shot – because of this area is very dangerous and mainly because the bridge has broken apart.

VO: The former JRA employee says it should never have taken this long – there are procedures in place to deal with emergency situations.

INSIDER: Even Joe Nhanhla – as early as Jan 2017, verbal instruction was issued, they were given permission to rehabilitate

VO: But despite promises of repairs in 2017, 2018 AND 2019 – the people of Alex are still waiting.

D – example of emergency – two years later not done - is that good enough?
T – it wasn’t done,
D – Why not
T - We don’t have a contractor for that bridge // the market not responsive as anticipated.

VO: By Chongo’s own admission, services are not being delivered because currently there is no approved panel specifically for bridge construction contractors.

Two bids have called for contractors to tender – while the first was cancelled due to irregularities in the bill of quantities, only a handful of bidders met the minimum company experience requirements.

The second bid, raised the bar even higher for company experience requirements, no bidders qualified - not even international companies nor contractors that have built over 200 bridges.

Our JRA source believes this is intentional.

INSIDER: the officials of JRA make very certain that when they put a tender out, they put it not to appoint, they know it is going to fail, // purposely they make the standards too high.

VO: An allegation Chongo denies.

D – nobody qualified - you don’t think the specs were too high
T – nature of the work – specialist work
D – Allegations kickbacks tender
T – how do I feel – it’s an allegation – it is not part of the JRA would want to be associated it

VO: That’s interesting – this is another snippet from the meeting between a potential contractor and a JRA official – the official explains how some contractors on the engineering consultants panel could get more work than others.

T – as it stands everyone, everyone who gets in to that panel will get something – one or two but some will then get four or five – so we’d want you get four or five.

VO: The JRA official in the meeting is none other than Thomas Chongo – head of planning.

DEVI: Is that your voice?
T: it could be my voice but I’ve never met to discuss these contracts
DEVI: but that is your voice – do you recall this meeting? normally it’s best to disclose now, at the beginning, because you know I’ve got more

VO: We played him another clip to help jog his memory. Here he explains how he would like his kickback paid.

T – It’s very straight forward, cash is king - no paper trail.
C – no paper trail
T – I, I prefer cash, it eliminates a lot of… yah, you know.

D - you prefer cash
T – I don’t what we were discussing but it had nothing to do with that.

VO: They also talk about minimising contact after the meeting

D – if this was something that was above board why minimise interaction?
T – um… beause
D - come on Thomas
T – it’s uhhh
D – because it’s not right
T – can I just have water

VO: In the recording, Chongo goes on to explain that the contractor should inflate the amount of hours in order to build in the kickback.

T – you then decide, ah know it’s 10 hours, then I’ll say before you submit make it 13 hours.
C – I think that’s very good

D – gonna get worse
T – no comment?
D – Now you got no comment

VO: He tried to explain that he had no influence over contracts, but then decided to take a different approach.

T – it could be many voices together
D- we altered it
T – have to ascertain it’s my voice.

VO: In 2018 already, we investigated the crumbling infrastructure at the Johannesburg Roads Agency – exposing internal struggles, alleged interference with tender allocations and even pre-payments made to contractors before work was done.

We alerted the Mayor to these irregularities, but fast forward 11 months and the forensic report is yet to be released.

We played Mayor Mashaba the recordings.

DEVI- How respond to HOD planning kickbacks
HM: …..This man is history in this administration.

VO: The city acted more shiftly this time round. Subsequent to our interview – Thomas Chongo has been suspended.

DEVI: Flags were raised last year about these tender allocation processes
HM: two reports… that are so damning…

VO: But these are reports that have yet to be released, because the JRA board, keep coming back with queries - delaying the implementation of the report’s recommendations.

HM: can’t accept delaying tactics
DEVI: Mayor they are playing games with you.
HM: gonna catch up with them
DEVI: 11 months... inaction
HM: JRA on radar no one come out unscathed.

LINK: And while the wheeling and dealing carries on at the JRA – relatively simply infrastructure repairs are delayed, putting disadvantage communities like this at risk – they the bear the brunt of corruption and kickbacks

DEVI: What if nothing is done
PETER: We are looking at possibly to some serious disasters, not only in terms of the cost in life, but to the cost to the economy
 
PROMOS

PROMO 1
VO: Joburg road infrastructure is crumbling with 707 substandard bridges in the City’s Roads Agency network.
HERMAN: Drive at own risk

PROMO 2
VO: We uncover corruption, mismanagement and alleged kickbacks in the Joburg Roads Agency that has contributed to the deterioration of the city’s roads infrastructure impacting on road users.


PROMO 3
VO: With 94% of Johannesburg’s bridges in a fair to extremely poor condition - we investigate corruption, kickbacks and mismanagement as insiders and experts lift the lid on the chaos.

T – we continuous monitor all the bridges we are concerned D – processes urgent today or tomorrow not end of year T – we look at it – if it becomes a threat – would closed it off D – not ER T – urgent – not Emergency situation as it stands. VO: But it seems even when it’s an emergency it’s not always dealt with urgently at the JRA. In November 2016, extreme flooding hit Johannesburg causing havoc across the city – at least 9 bridges collapsed. LINK: Bridges like this one – the Joe Nhlanhla Bridge in Alexandra were damaged, declared unsafe and closed. That was back in 2016… nothing has changed. VO: Adolph Marema is the ward councillor for this section of Alexandra. ADOLPH: 3000 to 4000 people passes – there’s more than 6 schools on the this other side // the taxi ranks are not this side – they are this side, so people from this side go this side to access to taxi rank, kids form this side goes to access schools VO: After doing a visual inspection of this bridge, Coetzee believes it’s fairly stable. PETER: There is not cracking, there’s been no movement, the concrete looks solid, there is no spalling or anything – except for the approach slabs and the ring walls which might need a bit of repair and the gabience that have fallen away – it’s fine. VO: Marema points out, it goes beyond the structure and inconvenience – residents are not safe. ADOLPH: once in a month we get reports of someone who has died, who has passed on, stabbed, mugged, shot – because of this area is very dangerous and mainly because the bridge has broken apart. VO: The former JRA employee says it should never have taken this long – there are procedures in place to deal with emergency situations. INSIDER: Even Joe Nhanhla – as early as Jan 2017, verbal instruction was issued, they were given permission to rehabilitate VO: But despite promises of repairs in 2017, 2018 AND 2019 – the people of Alex are still waiting. D – example of emergency – two years later not done - is that good enough? T – it wasn’t done, D – Why not T - We don’t have a contractor for that bridge // the market not responsive as anticipated. VO: By Chongo’s own admission, services are not being delivered because currently there is no approved panel specifically for bridge construction contractors. Two bids have called for contractors to tender – while the first was cancelled due to irregularities in the bill of quantities, only a handful of bidders met the minimum company experience requirements. The second bid, raised the bar even higher for company experience requirements, no bidders qualified - not even international companies nor contractors that have built over 200 bridges. Our JRA source believes this is intentional. INSIDER: the officials of JRA make very certain that when they put a tender out, they put it not to appoint, they know it is going to fail, // purposely they make the standards too high. VO: An allegation Chongo denies. D – nobody qualified - you don’t think the specs were too high T – nature of the work – specialist work D – Allegations kickbacks tender T – how do I feel – it’s an allegation – it is not part of the JRA would want to be associated it VO: That’s interesting – this is another snippet from the meeting between a potential contractor and a JRA official – the official explains how some contractors on the engineering consultants panel could get more work than others. T – as it stands everyone, everyone who gets in to that panel will get something – one or two but some will then get four or five – so we’d want you get four or five. VO: The JRA official in the meeting is none other than Thomas Chongo – head of planning. DEVI: Is that your voice? T: it could be my voice but I’ve never met to discuss these contracts DEVI: but that is your voice – do you recall this meeting? normally it’s best to disclose now, at the beginning, because you know I’ve got more VO: We played him another clip to help jog his memory. Here he explains how he would like his kickback paid. T – It’s very straight forward, cash is king - no paper trail. C – no paper trail T – I, I prefer cash, it eliminates a lot of… yah, you know. D - you prefer cash T – I don’t what we were discussing but it had nothing to do with that. VO: They also talk about minimising contact after the meeting D – if this was something that was above board why minimise interaction? T – um… beause D - come on Thomas T – it’s uhhh D – because it’s not right T – can I just have water VO: In the recording, Chongo goes on to explain that the contractor should inflate the amount of hours in order to build in the kickback. T – you then decide, ah know it’s 10 hours, then I’ll say before you submit make it 13 hours. C – I think that’s very good D – gonna get worse T – no comment? D – Now you got no comment VO: He tried to explain that he had no influence over contracts, but then decided to take a different approach. T – it could be many voices together D- we altered it T – have to ascertain it’s my voice. VO: In 2018 already, we investigated the crumbling infrastructure at the Johannesburg Roads Agency – exposing internal struggles, alleged interference with tender allocations and even pre-payments made to contractors before work was done. We alerted the Mayor to these irregularities, but fast forward 11 months and the forensic report is yet to be released. We played Mayor Mashaba the recordings. DEVI- How respond to HOD planning kickbacks HM: …..This man is history in this administration. VO: The city acted more shiftly this time round. Subsequent to our interview – Thomas Chongo has been suspended. DEVI: Flags were raised last year about these tender allocation processes HM: two reports… that are so damning… VO: But these are reports that have yet to be released, because the JRA board, keep coming back with queries - delaying the implementation of the report’s recommendations. HM: can’t accept delaying tactics DEVI: Mayor they are playing games with you. HM: gonna catch up with them DEVI: 11 months... inaction HM: JRA on radar no one come out unscathed. LINK: And while the wheeling and dealing carries on at the JRA – relatively simply infrastructure repairs are delayed, putting disadvantage communities like this at risk – they the bear the brunt of corruption and kickbacks DEVI: What if nothing is done PETER: We are looking at possibly to some serious disasters, not only in terms of the cost in life, but to the cost to the economy PROMOS PROMO 1 VO: Joburg road infrastructure is crumbling with 707 substandard bridges in the City’s Roads Agency network. HERMAN: Drive at own risk PROMO 2 VO: We uncover corruption, mismanagement and alleged kickbacks in the Joburg Roads Agency that has contributed to the deterioration of the city’s roads infrastructure impacting on road users. PROMO 3 VO: With 94% of Johannesburg’s bridges in a fair to extremely poor condition - we investigate corruption, kickbacks and mismanagement as insiders and experts lift the lid on the chaos. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): With only 6 % of the City of Johannesburg’s bridges in a good condition – who’s to blame? Carte Blanche investigates.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: - STORY CURRENTLY IN THE NEWS - BUT OTHER JOURNOS ARE REPORTING ON THE TRAFFIC DRAMA... - WE UNCOVER THE CORRUPTION AND MISMANAGEMENT BEHIND THE CURRENT STATE OF JHB's BRIDGES - VISUALS WILL BE SHOCKING - WE HAVE ACCESS TO A RECORDING PROVING KICKBACKS AND IMPLICATING A VERY SENIOR OFFICIAL AT THE JRA - GREAT OPPORTUNITY FOR CONFRONT WITH MAYOR HERMAN MASHABA AND A CHANCE TO DEMAND THAT REPORT HE PROMISED ALMOST A YEAR AGO - HE IS SO SET ON ROOTING OUT CORRUPTION BUT APPARENTLY NOT SO MUCH WHEN IT INVOLVES COALITION PARTNERS.....
metadata.Summary: 94% of Johannesburg’s bridges are in a fair to extremely poor condition. City Mayor Herman Mashaba would like you to believe he inherited the problem and that it’s the ANC’s fault. We beg to differ. There is proof that Mayor Mashaba is not free from blame – he is in part responsible for the current situation. We speak to insiders and experts to get to the bottom of the bridge fiasco, putting Mayor Mashaba on the spot.
metadata.Further information: THE BRIDGE CONDITION STATISTICS ARE NOT NEW – 94% of BRIDGES HAVE BEEN IN A TERRIBLE STATE SINCE 2013! JRA HISTORY RELATED TO MAINTENANCE A 7 yr plan was done in 2013 to address the bridge situation. JRA engineers worked with SANRAL engineers to come up with a game plan to address the maintenance issues and implement a plan of action to do repairs where needed and to maintain the good bridges. The city would need R700 000 per bridge to maintain the good ones. R4 million to bring the fair ones up to very good status. R15 million from poor to very good. R70 million from very poor to very good. The JRA team under Sean Phillips and then CEO (not sure of spelling) had implemented a plan with targets in place – in 2014, 2015 & 2016 those targets were met. ENTER MASHABA & COALITION GOVERNMENT In 2017 & 2018 no targets were met. NOT A SINGLE BRIDGE WAS MAINTAINED OR REPAIRED. That budget is believed to have gone back to treasury. SO DEAR MAYOR MASHABA, YOU CAN’T BLAME THE ANC FOR THIS ONE…. During November 2016 there were massive storms and flooding in Johannesburg. 15 bridges were closed as a result. Today they are still closed. WHY THE LACK OF ACTION? Internal struggles to get tenders awarded to the “RIGHT” consultants and engineers. Links back to our JRA story and how coalition politics impacts on the running of the municipality and service delivery. In the case of the 15 bridges that were closed in 2016, Mashaba will claim that an EIA needs to be done and a contractor needs to be appointed. THIS IS NOT THE CASE – in an emergency situations, no EIA’s are necessary. The repairs for a number of the bridges could have been done internally by the JRA – the expertise and resources were available – but it seems tenderpreneuring got in the way of service delivery. An example is the John Hlanhla bridge in Alex – it needs to have the embankment filled up and secured. Still hasn’t happened. THOMAS CHONGA – ENGINEER & HEAD OF PLANNING: JRA – ALSO TAKES KICKBACKS We are in possession of an audio recording where Chongo details & negotiates his kick back from consultants – he explains how it needs to be done. I am negotiating with the source to be able to use it on air – if not we’ll find ways of incorporating the allegations. Chonga has managed to get 3 bridge contracts awarded to one company – OJM. This is irregular as the JRA used to rotate contracts between consultants – one for you, then one for you, then one for you. This isn’t happening any more. As the head of planning, Chonga, has acted outside of his scope and interfered in Supply Chain Management. Rumour has it that he was dismissed from Ekurhuleni for similar mismanagement – need to confirm. SIDE STEPPING TENDER PROCESSES Since MAshaba’s coalition government has been in place no contracts have been awarded through the normal tender process. Apparently the tender specification are so ridiculous that no one meets the requirements – not even big companies like Stefanotti. This in turn opens the door for Regulation 32 – if no suitable contractor submitted a tender, the municipality may directly contract a contractor currently being used by another municipality. Ekurhuleni uses Khato Civils who were the subject of our last JRA story that exposed the irregular prepayment of R23 million that was made to them. Even JRA employees raised concerns about the tender specifications being unrealistic, but it was pushed through. Currently the JRA are claiming to come up with new strategies – yet new data has been generated. Even Gauteng Province has offered assistance to attend to the bridges and road maintenance, but the delays according to insiders are simply the allocation of contracts that stand to benefit corrupt individuals with in the JRA – the expertise and plan exists internally but is not being used. M2 CLOSURE FOR REPAIRS Mayor Mashaba is masquerading this contract as a display of his government delivering on promises, doing the maintenance and repairs that the ANC was incapable of. They seem to have chosen the bridge that would draw the most attention and would also deliver the most contracts – ignoring bridges that could literally collapse any day. QUEEN ELIZABETH BRIDGE – BRAAMFONTEIN Traffic from the M2 is now being diverted along this bridge. This is a very bad move. The pictures tell a very dire story. Trains also move underneath this bridge, structural engineers have raised concerns, yet it has been ignored. AND IGNORING BRIDGES THAT COULD REALLY MAKE A DIFFERENCE TO COMMUNITIES: MZIMHLOPHE PEDESTRIAN BRIDGE This bridge gives school kids access from their neighbourhood to the school – it’s a 300m distance over the bridge. It remains closed because it is unsafe, they now have to travel a 9km distance to get to school. VIUSALLY IT’s HORRIFIC! PEOPLE ARE GOING TO GO MENTAL AND WE ALL SHOULD BE REALLY CONCERNED ABOUT WHERE WE DRIVE… IT’s LITERALLY DISASTERS WAITING TO HAPPEN!! • I HAVE DOCUMENTS AND REPORTS TO BACK UP THESE CLAIMS
